title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LA0LD_1RB0RD_1LE0RF_0LB0RB_1RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LA0LD_1RB0RD_1LE0RF_0LB0RB_1RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: It does not halt, proved in Lean with native_decide for the long fixed computations. The configuration C k = 0^inf A> 0 (1010001000100)^k X, with X a fixed stretch of 222,182 cells, goes to C (k+1) in 184k + 3,029,040 steps for every k ≥ 1, and the run from blank tape reaches C 7 at step 16,730,681,219 (checked chunk by chunk with a block simulator proved correct in Lean). Theorem nonhalting in lean/Reach.lean.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The three symbolic passes over the blocks
claims.text: With R any tape: 0^inf A> 0 (1010001000100)^(n+1) R reaches 0^inf (0101010010001)^(n+1) 1 B> R in 37n+38 steps; 0^inf (0101010010001)^(n+1) E> 0 R reaches 0^inf (0101010010001)^(n+1) 0 1 1 B> R in 92n+99 steps, passing after its first 55n+57 steps through 0^inf A> 0 1 0 (1000100010010)^(n+1) R at the left end (pass3). For every n and R.

claims.title: Runs on a window never look further left
claims.text: A run on a finite window of cells that never moves left of the window (wsteps, a list simulator that fails when the head would leave the window) is a run of the machine with any tape at all on the left.

claims.title: The two excursions into X
claims.text: Entering the fixed stretch X (222,182 cells, lean/Data.lean) from the blocks, the head comes back out after 1,517,479 steps in state E onto a 0, leaving a stretch r1; entering r1 the next time, it comes back after 1,511,551 steps, leaving a stretch that, with the two cells the last pass writes in front of it, is one more block followed by X again.

claims.title: One period of the bouncer, for every number of blocks
claims.text: With C k = 0^inf A> 0 (1010001000100)^k X 0^inf: C (n+1) reaches C (n+2) in exactly 184n + 3,029,224 steps, for every n. So from any C (m+1) the machine runs for ever, and if the run from blank tape reaches some C (m+1), the machine does not halt.

claims.title: A block simulator, proved correct
claims.text: The tape cut into blocks of 16 cells, and a table that says, for each state, block and side of entry, what the machine does in the block until the head leaves it. Each table entry is computed by a run on the block's cells that is proved to be a run of the machine whatever lies outside (brun_ok); the simulator msim looks up one entry per block crossing, and chkF_ok turns a successful check of a run of exactly t steps (macro steps, then single steps) into steps t ... = some ....

claims.title: The run from blank tape reaches C 7 at step 16,730,681,219
claims.text: The run is cut into eight chunks of about 2.09×109 steps at configurations dumped by the C simulator (lean/Bound.lean); each chunk is checked by the block simulator with native_decide (about 3 minutes each, lean/Chunk1.lean … lean/Chunk8.lean), the table by tblOk (20 s). The C simulator only proposes the boundaries; Lean checks every step between them. Chained: steps 16730681219 init = some (C 7).

claims.title: The machine never halts from blank tape
claims.text: nonhalting : ¬ HaltsFromBlank, from reach_C7 and nonhalt_of_reach. It rests on Lean's kernel and on compiled evaluation for the native_decide facts (the two excursions into X, the closing equality, the block table and the eight chunks).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: py/lturn.c runs 1011 steps without a halt and logs every 50th left turn; from sweep 49,300 on (step 1.68×1010) the left turn is the left end and the step counts of the turns follow a quadratic exactly (third differences 0): left end −2 cells per sweep, right end +4.5. At 1011 steps the tape spans cells −71,625 to 382,423.

claims.title: The rightward sweep over the Q encoding is a block transducer
claims.text: In state D, moving right, the head crosses each of the blocks 1000, 100100, 1001000, 10010100, 100101000 in state D without looking past it, so it crosses any word made of them block by block. A building block for the earlier phase; the period proof above does not use it.

claims.title: Before the bouncer: a turning point that runs out and back in epochs
claims.text: Up to step 1.67×10<sup>10</sup> the leftward sweeps do not all reach the left end: the cell where they turn moves right, about 7 cells per sweep, until it meets the right end (sweeps 150, 650, 2,550, 9,500, 35,550, right end at 774, 3,024, 11,648, 42,923, 160,189 cells), then runs back to the left end (sweeps 250, 950, 3,600, 13,350, 49,300). Each epoch is about 3.7 times longer than the one before. After the fifth return the configuration is C 7 and the bouncer above takes over.

explainer.lede: No. For its first 1.67×1010 steps this machine goes through five ever longer epochs; then it settles into an exact repeating pattern, a bouncer: the head sweeps between the two ends, and every two sweeps one more block of 13 cells appears on the left while a fixed stretch of 222,182 cells is carried along. Lean proves that the pattern repeats for ever and, chunk by chunk, that the run from blank tape gets there.

facts.text: One period, for every k: 184k + 3,029,040 steps.
The step at which the run reaches C 7, checked in eight chunks.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.538).
After 109 steps the tape spans 57,599 cells (252 left of the start, 49,179 right), with a density of 1s of 0.36.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

The head, in state A, stands on the leftmost cell. Then come k copies of the block 10 1000 1000 100 (13 cells), then a stretch X of 222,182 cells that is always the same. X is what is left of the earlier epochs: an irregular record of 10s, 100s and 1000s that the sweeps rewrite on the way out and restore on the way back.

Over one period (two sweeps) the left end moves 4 cells left, one block is added, and X ends up 9 cells further right, so the right end grows 9 cells per period. The time per period grows by 184 steps per block, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the bouncer signature.

sections.heading: One period, piece by piece
html: Over the blocks the machine is easy to follow symbolically, for any number of them; inside X it is not, but X is a fixed string, so the run there is simply computed. The two kinds of piece meet at the boundary between the blocks and X:

excursion 11 B> XE> 0 r11,517,479

excursion 20 1 1 B> r1E> 0 r21,511,551
pass 3 (left)(0101010010001)^(n+1) E> 0 r2A> 0 1 0 (1000100010010)^(n+1) r255n + 57

and 1 0 (1000100010010)^(n+1) r2 = (1010001000100)^(n+2) X: the period ends at C (n+2), after 184n + 3,029,224 steps in all. In each excursion the head never moves left of the cells written next to it (1, or 0 1 1), so what the excursion does does not depend on n. The passes are proved by Lean's kernel for every n; the excursions and the final equality are evaluated with native_decide, about 3 million steps on a list of 222,000 cells.

sections.heading: How it gets there: five epochs
html: Before the bouncer the leftward sweeps do not always reach the left end. The cell where they turn back (green below) creeps right, about 7 cells per sweep, while the right end (red) gains 4.5 cells per sweep; when the turning point catches up with the right end it runs back to the left end, and the next epoch starts. Five epochs, each about 3.7 times longer than the last, end at sweeps 250, 950, 3,600, 13,350 and 49,300. After the fifth the turning point stays at the left end: the tape is then C 7, and the period above repeats from there on.
Logged every 200 sweeps by py/lturn.c up to 1011 steps (84,927 sweeps). After sweep 49,300 the step counts of the turns follow a quadratic exactly.

sections.heading: Why it never halts
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. State F is entered only from D reading 1 (D1 = 0RF), so a halt needs the head in state D on 1 1. In the bouncer phase this never happens: the period is proved for every number of blocks, and the run over X is the same every time. Before it, Lean checks the whole run of 16,730,681,219 steps from blank tape, in eight chunks of about 2×109 steps: the C simulator proposes the configurations at the chunk boundaries, and a block simulator proved correct in Lean (blocks of 16 cells, one table lookup per block crossing) checks each chunk, with native_decide.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: The result: nonhalting : ¬ HaltsFromBlank (lean/Reach.lean). Lean, kernel: pass1, pass2, pass3 (lean/Pass.lean), wsteps_over (lean/Window.lean), the block simulator and its correctness chkF_ok (lean/Block.lean), finalF_ok (lean/Final.lean), dsweep (lean/Sweep.lean). Lean, native_decide: w1_ok, w2_ok, close (lean/Period.lean, a few seconds), tblOk (lean/TblOk.lean, 20 s), chunk1 … chunk8 (lean/Chunk1.lean … lean/Chunk8.lean, about 3 minutes each). Trusted (C), not needed for the proof: no halt in 1011 steps (py/lturn.c). Heuristic: the epoch description before the bouncer.

family: bouncer after epochs (exact period with a fixed 222k-cell stretch)
summary: Does not halt (Lean, with native_decide): after five epochs it becomes an exact bouncer, C k -> C (k+1) with a fixed stretch of 222,182 cells, reached at step 16,730,681,219.
